3.0.s.en: (3) The dung gate and the fountain gate

3.0.0.en: Malchiah the son of Rechab: he was of the tribe of Rechab, who were not Jews but lived beside them in peace, and Jeremiah mentioned them as an example of obedience to the commands of their chief (Jer 35). The dung gate, as we mentioned in (ch. 2:13), lies south of the city of Jerusalem and east of the valley gate, and the dung of animals was thrown out from it. Therefore this gate signifies purity, that is, a person's being rid of all his evils and impurities, which the waste signifies.

3.0.1.en: This gate was repaired by one of the great men named Malchiah the son of Rechab, who was ruler of a district called the district of Beth-haccerem.

3.0.2.en: This shows the concern of the great men for repairing the wall and the gates, and of course the rest of their families followed them, so the work was a popular work in which all the people took part, the great and those who were not great.

3.1.0.en: The district of Mizpah: a place outside Jerusalem, lying near it, within the tribe of Benjamin.

3.1.1.en: The fountain gate: called the gate of the spring, and it is opposite En-rogel. We mentioned about it in (2:14) that it lies east of the dung gate and beside it is the pool of Siloam, which was formed from the spring of water, that is, this spring flows into it. The pool of Siloam is in fact an open channel in which the water runs down with a gentle slope and finally flows into a pool called the old pool or the pool of Siloam, which is mentioned in the New Testament, and in which the man born blind washed (Jn 9:6). The spring signifies the Holy Spirit, since no one digs it but it comes forth naturally, just as God's grace gives us the work of the Holy Spirit in us. The spring or the water signifies the sacrament of Baptism, so this gate signifies the Holy Spirit and Baptism.

3.1.2.en: Shallun repaired this gate, he and his household, then repaired the wall beside this gate as far as the king's garden, called the garden, which is a wide area of gardens belonging to the king, and it extended after that to a stair called the stair of the city of David, and because Jerusalem is built on hills, stairs are many in it. The city of David is a part of Jerusalem called by this name, and sometimes the name city of David is applied to all of Jerusalem. Shallun was ruler of the district of Mizpah, which is a place outside Jerusalem, and this shows the concern of the Jews in all the region of Judea surrounding Jerusalem for repairing the wall of the city of God, just as non-Jews living beside them, such as the Rechabites, also cooperated in this great work.

3.2.0.en: The district of Beth-zur: a suburb lying outside Jerusalem, 20 miles south of Jerusalem. The sepulchres of David: it was the custom to place tombs outside cities, because whoever touches a dead person becomes unclean, but tombs were set up for the kings, who were of the descendants of David, inside the city of Jerusalem.

3.2.1.en: The pool that was made: King Hezekiah made it to store water in it after he stopped up the springs outside the city of Jerusalem so that the Assyrians who were besieging his city at that time would not use them.

3.2.2.en: The house of the mighty: where the military commanders of David's army dwelt, and this area was afterward turned into army barracks and storehouses for weapons.

3.2.3.en: The complementarity of the two tasks of building the wall appears here: after Shallun, Nehemiah the son of Azbuk repaired the wall opposite the tombs of David, the pool that was made and the house of the mighty. Thus the repair of the wall extends from the south of Jerusalem toward its east as far as the water gate mentioned in (v. 26). By this we find that the direction of the repair began from the north and goes counterclockwise until it finally reaches the north again at the end of this chapter.

3.3.0.en: Keilah: a city lying in the plain of Judah near the border of the tribe of Judah with the Philistines. The Levites under Rehum also took part in repairing the wall, as did Hashabiah, who was ruler of the city of Keilah.

3.4.0.en: And after Hashabiah, ruler of half the district of Keilah, his relatives repaired under Bavai, ruler of the other half of the district of Keilah.

3.4.1.en: That is, all the inhabitants of the city were concerned to take part in this work.

3.5.0.en: The armory: storehouses of weapons to which the city resorts in time of war.

3.5.1.en: The turning: a corner in the wall of the city.

3.5.2.en: A group from the city of Mizpah came forward under one of its rulers, Ezer, to repair a second section of the wall, other than that repaired by their brethren from the city of Mizpah mentioned in (v. 15). This section was opposite a stair at the armory in the corner of the city.

3.6.0.en: After the Mizpah group, whom Ezer led, Baruch and those who followed him came forward with great zeal, distinguished from the other groups working in repairing the wall, and he repaired from the corner of the city to the door of the house of Eliashib the high priest, that is, the chief of the priests.

3.6.1.en: May you come forward toward God in earnest worship with care, whether in your prayers or your readings. Make a plan for yourself with your spiritual father and keep to it, and try to seize every opportunity to grow in your worship. This of course will stir your love toward God, and He will reward you with many things, and will open your heart with love for those around you, so that you serve them faithfully and experience new depths in the love of God.

3.7.0.en: The love of Meremoth and the group with him appears in their concern to repair a second section of the wall other than that which they repaired in (v. 4). This section lies in the eastern part of the temple and extends from the door of the high priest, and of the priests next to him, to the end of these buildings, which were attached to the wall and faced the valley of Kidron, which lies outside Jerusalem.

3.7.1.en: It is noticed that Meremoth's group were not content to repair the wall opposite their houses, but out of their zeal repaired another part that needed repair, and this shows their activity, which God greatly esteems. What they repaired in (v. 4) was at the fish gate in the north of the city, but the second section in this verse was at the east of the city.

3.8.0.en: The plain: a depression in the earth, that is, a plain, or a valley, and this name is applied to the southern part of the valley of the river Jordan.

3.8.1.en: Some of the workers in the temple and some of the priests lived in the plain of the Jordan, that is, the plain surrounding Jerusalem, also called the district, and these priests came and took part in repairing the wall of Jerusalem. This confirms the priests' sense that repairing the wall was a holy work, because it was connected with the holy city Jerusalem, in which was the temple of the Lord.

3.9.0.en: He continues to mention those who took part in the repair, mentioning Benjamin and Hashub, who repaired it, with their followers, opposite their houses, and after them Azariah the son of Maaseiah repaired. This shows that the repair of the wall was a popular work in which every person took part for God's sake, and to protect himself and his city. This signifies the duty of every person to put right any wrongs he meets and to do the good that is available to him, so that he may have a share in the Kingdom of Heaven, becoming a true member of the Church through his love, his service and his doing of good.

3.9.1.en: When you find an opportunity to do good, do not neglect it, for God is the One who gave it to you so that you may show your love for Him, and so become a true son and obtain His many mercies.

3.10.0.en: The zeal of some persons in repairing the wall appears here: after they completed the portion assigned to them by Nehemiah, they went back and repaired another section. Among them was Binnui the son of Henadad, mentioned in this verse, who is also called Bavai the son of Henadad, mentioned in (v. 18). In this verse he repaired a part of the wall at a corner in the wall, opposite which was a turning, that is, a small lane that was well known in Jerusalem.

3.10.1.en: It is noticed that Binnui, or Bavai, is ruler of half the district of Keilah, that is, the rulers were concerned with repairing the wall and not only the people, and this confirms that all classes of the people cared for the work of God.

3.11.0.en: The tower: a tower set up to defend the king's house.

3.11.1.en: The upper house of the king: most likely the old house of David.

3.11.2.en: The court of the prison: a prison attached to the king's house, in which were probably put those who offended against the king personally or against his servants and those who worked with him.

3.11.3.en: The Jews continue repairing the wall from the fountain gate toward the water gate, and Palal repairs opposite the corner at which Binnui, mentioned in the previous verse, ended, and also opposite the tower attached to the upper house of the king and the court of the prison. After Palal, another person called Pedaiah the son of Parosh repaired.

3.11.4.en: It is noticed that the Holy Bible takes care to mention the name of each one who repaired the wall, to show God's concern for the work of every person who offers Him service, so He records it in His book, as a proclamation that He records every good work and rewards its doer in the Kingdom of Heaven.

3.11.5.en: Be confident that every good thing you do has value before God, even if others neglect it, despise it or reject it. God thanks you for what you have done and records it with Him so that you may enjoy His reward in eternal life. So continue doing good, whatever the obstacles.

3.12.s.en: (4) The water gate and the horse gate

3.12.0.en: The Nethinim: they are the Gibeonites who deceived Joshua long ago, so he promised not to destroy them, and when he discovered that they dwelt near him, he made them work in the service of the temple, gathering wood and drawing water. Ophel: a part of the hill lying south-east of Jerusalem.

3.12.1.en: The water gate: the one that leads to the spring of Gihon, which is the main source of fresh water supplying the city of Jerusalem. Opposite the fountain gate there is a large courtyard inside the city in which people gathered either to hear the Holy Scriptures, as Ezra did (Neh 8:1), or in which booths were set up on the days of the Feast of Tabernacles (Neh 8:16). There is an opinion that the water gate is not a gate of the city but a gate of the palace attached to the temple of the Lord. The next group in the repair is the group of the Nethinim, who repaired the wall at the water gate and the outer tower. This shows that all classes of those who worked in the temple took part in repairing the wall, not only the priests and Levites but also the Nethinim; not only the Jews took part but also non-Jews attached to them, for God accepts the service of all and their love, and Christ came for the salvation of all mankind.

3.12.2.en: The water gate signifies the word of God, which overflows upon everyone who cares for it and satisfies him and works in him and through him. This gate was sound and did not need repair, and it signifies the steadfastness of the word of God.

3.12.3.en: Do not despise anyone's service, whatever his position, race or religion, for God welcomes and rejoices in all, and He is the One who works in all to draw them to Himself.

3.13.0.en: The work extended after the water gate toward the east, and the Tekoites repaired a part of the wall. This part is a second section, for after they repaired the first part mentioned in (v. 5) they came forward to repair another part. This shows their activity despite the slackness of their leaders in this work, which did not affect their activity. This new part was opposite the great tower and Ophel.

3.14.0.en: The horse gate: it lies on the eastern side of the city, north of the water gate, and through it the king's horses entered their stables. It is noticed that the king's palace was near this gate, because the horse gate was near the temple, and beside it were the dwellings of the priests, so they took care to repair it and the wall above it. And because horses take part in war, they represented at that time military strength; therefore the gate of the temple signifies striving and victory.

3.15.s.en: (5) The east gate and the gate Miphkad

3.15.0.en: The east gate: it lies on the eastern side of the city opposite the temple, and it is the first gate opened in the city at sunrise and is considered the main entrance of the temple, and it was later called the Beautiful gate (Acts 3:2). The people continued to take part in repairing the wall: Zadok repaired opposite his house, and after him Shemaiah repaired opposite his house, and Shemaiah was the one responsible for guarding the east gate, for his dwelling was opposite this gate. The east gate signifies the Sun of Righteousness, since it is the first gate from which the sun appears; therefore it signifies the Incarnation of Christ, the Sun of Righteousness, who was born in the east, and it also signifies His Second Coming, which will come from the east.

3.16.0.en: The repair continues after the east gate, moving toward the north. Hananiah and Hanun repaired, and after them Meshullam repaired opposite his house. Perhaps Meshullam was one of the priests and had a position among them, so a chamber was given to him, that is, a dwelling place inside the temple, and he repaired the wall opposite this chamber.

3.16.1.en: The activity of Hanun is noticed, for he repaired a second section: he first repaired the valley gate (v. 13), and although the Holy Bible mentions that he was the sixth, it most likely means that he was sixth in order among his brothers, not the firstborn or after him. He was filled with more zeal and activity than the rest of his brothers, so he repaired two sections, and it is not mentioned that his brothers repaired anything of the wall, so he may have been the only one who cared for the holy work.

3.16.2.en: Let no one despise your youth, but be positive and do every good you are able to do, for God is able to work through your weakness greater things than through anyone, so that He is glorified through you and you enjoy fellowship with Him.

3.17.0.en: The house of the Nethinim: most likely a house set up to manage the affairs of the Nethinim in the temple, because the Nethinim lived outside Jerusalem and near it.

3.17.1.en: The gate Miphkad (the gate of numbering): the armies returning from war entered through it, and the king stood at this gate numbering his returning armies to learn the extent of their victory or defeat before the enemies. This gate lies in the east toward the north and near the king's house, and it is the last of the gates before reaching the sheep gate with which we began.

3.17.2.en: The work on the wall extends after the east gate as we approach the gate Miphkad, and Malchiah repairs. The Scripture mentions that he was the goldsmith's son, that is, some of the goldsmiths lived east of the city opposite this gate and others lived in the west near the old gate, as we mentioned (v. 8). The merchants also took part in repairing the wall and the gate Miphkad as far as the going up of the turning. As we mentioned, there were many stairs in the city because it is built on hills, and it seems that this stair led to a well-known lane in the city.

3.17.3.en: The gate Miphkad signifies judgment, because the king stands in person to number his soldiers returning from war, just as the King of kings, our Lord Jesus Christ, will judge the whole world, to separate those victorious over Satan from those who yielded to their lusts.

3.18.0.en: It is mentioned here that the remaining part of the wall between the going up of the turning and the sheep gate was repaired by the goldsmiths and merchants, in addition to what they had previously repaired in the wall; they used their strength and their money to complete this holy work.

3.18.1.en: We also notice the concern of some classes, such as the goldsmiths and merchants, for repairing the remaining parts between the repaired sections of the wall, for parts might remain between what the different classes repaired, so they went along the wall to find any parts that had been neglected in order to repair them.

3.18.2.en: Be a helper to those around you to complete their work and service, even if your name does not appear or you receive no honor from people; but God greatly esteems all your good works and blesses them.

3.18.3.en: It is noticed that the twelve gates have spiritual meanings, all of which revolve around Christ, as appears in what follows:

3.18.4.en: 1- The sheep gate: signifies Christ, the Lamb incarnate for the redemption of mankind.

3.18.5.en: 2- The fish gate: signifies service and the gathering of souls to faith in Christ.

3.18.6.en: 3- The gate of Ephraim: signifies blessing, since Ephraim was the largest of the tribes in number, for through Christ the Redeemer we have received all blessings.

3.18.7.en: 4- The prison gate: signifies Christ the Redeemer, who freed us from the prison of sin and its bondage and gave us the glorious liberty of the children of God.

3.18.8.en: 5- The old gate: signifies the eternal Christ, everlasting, who is before all worlds, the Ancient of Days, the Creator of all things and the Renewer of our nature.

3.18.9.en: 6- The valley gate: signifies that salvation is within the Church, which Jerusalem signifies, and whoever goes outside Jerusalem falls into the valley of the son of Hinnom, that is, Gehenna. So through Christ the Redeemer inside the Church we obtain salvation by the Holy Sacraments and the means of grace.

3.18.10.en: 7- The dung gate: signifies purity, since the unclean waste is thrown out from it. Through Christ the Redeemer we obtain purity and cleanness in the Holy Sacraments.

3.18.11.en: 8- The fountain gate: signifies the Holy Spirit, who works in us and overflows from us, and through Him we receive new life through the sacrament of Baptism, so that we are born anew in Christ the Savior.

3.18.12.en: 9- The water gate: signifies Christ, the Word of God, who works in His children.

3.18.13.en: 10- The horse gate: signifies spiritual striving and victory over Satan by the power of Christ.

3.18.14.en: 11- The east gate: signifies Christ, the Sun of Righteousness, incarnate for our redemption and coming in His Second Coming to glorify His children.

3.18.15.en: 12- The gate Miphkad: signifies judgment and the recompense of every person according to his works by Christ the Judge.

3.18.16.en: So we notice that we began with Christ the Redeemer on the Cross and ended with Christ the Judge, for Christ is the Alpha and the Omega, the Beginning and the End.

3.18.17.en: A final note in this chapter: the name of Nehemiah is not mentioned among those who repaired the wall, because he was responsible for directing and organizing the different classes in this work, and this administration is a great work that takes a long time and is harder than the work of repair, since without it the wall would not be completed. For coordinating the work and encouraging it, arranging the defense of the wall against the enemies, and supporting and caring for those taking part in the repair is a work that surpasses all works.

3.18.18.en: The enemies' opposition to the building of the wall
